I use a rule of abstraction that I can't exactly remember the origin of. Basically, there are two kinds of feedback you can get. One is, "this planning is tedious and meticulous, and I feel like I'm planning so much that I'm half-doing the work". This feedback means you should step up, and try to chunk larger pieces of work at a time and plan less.

The other kind is when you go to start doing the thing you need to do, and you hit unexpected snags, or you feel confused, or you aren't sure how to start. This means you should step down, and try to break out the steps of your plan into smaller steps.

Really, no matter what "system" of planning you use, it's vulnerable to these mistakes (too low level or too high level). I've found that trying to understand your frustrations and productivity issues as feedback about what EXACTLY is wrong with your plan tends to help me, no matter what organizational system I'm working in.
